#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-run every check of the stage-2 statement gate pack and write the elaboration log.
# Read-only: `lean` on each file against the olean snapshot (no -o), python3 -I for the scripts.
S="$1"; WT="$S/wt-g2"; OL="$S/oleans-f7"; O="$S/gate-stage2"; LOG="$O/elaboration.log"
el() { bash "$S/tools/leanelab.sh" "$WT" "$OL" "$1" 2>&1; }
san() { sed "s|$O/|<OUT>/|g; s|$S/|<S>/|g"; }
python3 -I "$O/work/mkprobes.py" "$O" >&2
summ() { # file output exit
  local e w s o
  e=$(grep -c ': error' <<<"$2"); w=$(grep -c ': warning' <<<"$2")
  s=$(grep -c "declaration uses 'sorry'" <<<"$2"); o=$(grep -c ': warning' <<<"$2" | awk -v s="$s" '{print $1 - s}')
  echo "  exit $3 | errors $e | warnings $w | of which \`declaration uses 'sorry'\` $s | other warnings $o"
}
{
echo "# Stage-2 statement gate: elaboration log"
echo
echo "Tool: \`bash <S>/tools/leanelab.sh <S>/wt-g2 <S>/oleans-f7 <file>\` (direct \`lean\`, no \`-o\`,"
echo "no olean written). Worktree: the read-only campaign-tip checkout \`wt-g2\`; olean snapshot"
echo "\`oleans-f7\` (all of TCSlib, \`TCSlib/Programs\` included, and Mathlib). Toolchain:"
echo "\`$(cat "$WT/lean-toolchain")\`. <OUT> is the pack's output directory; <S> the scratchpad."
echo "Run: $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC')."
echo "In the repository the files map as: <OUT>/{Stage2,NDSlice,LanguageExtensions}.lean ->"
echo "audits/evidence/stage2-gate/<Name>.lean.txt; <OUT>/probes/<P>.lean ->"
echo "audits/evidence/stage2-gate/probes/<P>.lean.txt; <OUT>/work/<script> (cutcheck.py, stmtdiff.py,"
echo "names.py, cited.py, widths.py, mkprobes.py, runall.sh and the two probe tails) ->"
echo "audits/evidence/stage2-gate/scripts/<script>; <OUT>/work/lint.py is"
echo "scripts/campaign_style_lint.py with its ROOT line pointed at a copy of the three files."
echo
echo "## 1. The three proposed files"
for f in Stage2 NDSlice LanguageExtensions; do
  out=$(el "$O/$f.lean"); ex=$?
  echo; echo "### $f.lean ($(wc -l < "$O/$f.lean" | tr -d ' ') lines)"; summ "$f" "$out" "$ex"
  echo '```'; san <<<"$out"; echo '```'
done
echo
echo "## 2. Cut checks: each landing module of Stage2.lean in exactly its own import closure"
echo
echo "\`python3 -I <OUT>/work/cutcheck.py <OUT>/Stage2.lean <S>/wt-g2 <OUT>/work/cut\` writes, for"
echo "each part, a file holding the imports of the part's import closure and the bodies of the parts"
echo "in that closure, in file order (the method of \`scripts/vendor_afm26/closurecheck.py\`). Each is"
echo "elaborated on its own."
echo '```'
rm -rf "$O/work/cut"; (cd "$O/work" && python3 -I "$O/work/cutcheck.py" "$O/Stage2.lean" "$WT" "$O/work/cut") | san
echo '```'
for f in "$O"/work/cut/*.check.lean; do
  out=$(el "$f"); ex=$?
  echo "* \`$(basename "$f")\`:"; summ x "$out" "$ex"
done
echo
echo "## 3. Semantic sanity probes (evidence only; not landing material)"
for f in Stage2Sanity LanguageExtensionsSanity; do
  out=$(el "$O/probes/$f.lean"); ex=$?
  n=$(grep -c '^example' "$O/probes/$f.lean")
  echo; echo "### probes/$f.lean: the unit plus $n \`example\`s, each by \`rfl\`, \`decide\`, a term or a short tactic proof"
  summ x "$out" "$ex"
  echo '```'; san <<<"$out" | grep -v "declaration uses 'sorry'" ; echo "(the sorry warnings are those of the unit)"; echo '```'
done
echo
echo "Negative controls (deliberately false copies, deleted afterwards; each must fail):"
for n in neg1 neg2 neg3; do
  out=$(el "$O/work/$n.lean"); ex=$?
  echo "* \`$n\`: exit $ex, errors $(grep -c ': error' <<<"$out"): $(grep ': error' <<<"$out" | san | head -1 | cut -c1-120)"
done
echo "  (neg1: \`emit\` of a nonzero cell claimed to emit \`[false]\`; neg2: \`half\` of -3 claimed"
echo "  to be -1; neg3: \`inBitVal [false, true] 1\` claimed to be 0.)"
echo
echo "## 4. Style lint (\`scripts/campaign_style_lint.py\`, its ROOT pointed at a copy of the units)"
echo '```'
rm -rf "$O/work/lintroot"; mkdir -p "$O/work/lintroot/units"; cp "$O"/Stage2.lean "$O"/NDSlice.lean "$O"/LanguageExtensions.lean "$O/work/lintroot/units/"
(cd "$O/work" && python3 -I "$O/work/lint.py" units) | san
echo '```'
echo "The one WARN is Stage2.lean, an elaboration unit that lands as six modules (part sizes in the pack)."
echo
echo "## 5. Line widths (characters, not bytes)"
echo '```'
python3 -I "$O/work/widths.py" "$O/Stage2.lean" "$O/NDSlice.lean" "$O/LanguageExtensions.lean" | san
echo '```'
echo
echo "## 6. Name screen: the units' declarations against every declaration of TCSlib"
echo '```'
python3 -I "$O/work/names.py" "$O/Stage2.lean" "$O/NDSlice.lean" "$O/LanguageExtensions.lean" "$WT" | san
echo '```'
echo "Positive control: a file declaring \`WordRAM.startMem\` (the draft's name) and \`Light.Compiler.sim\`:"
echo '```'
python3 -I "$O/work/names.py" "$O/work/screen_ctrl.lean" "$WT" | san
echo '```'
echo
echo "## 7. Cited names: every backticked identifier of each unit's comments, as \`#check @…\`"
for spec in "Stage2:WordRAM Light Light.Compiler Turing Complexity" "NDSlice:Turing Turing.NDTM Turing.MultiTapeTM" "LanguageExtensions:Light Light.Compiler"; do
  f=${spec%%:*}; ops=${spec#*:}
  python3 -I "$O/work/cited.py" "$O/$f.lean" > "$O/work/cited_$f.txt"
  { cat "$O/$f.lean"; echo; echo "open $ops"; while read -r t; do echo "#check @$t"; done < "$O/work/cited_$f.txt"; } > "$O/work/cite_$f.lean"
  out=$(el "$O/work/cite_$f.lean")
  echo; echo "### $f: $(wc -l < "$O/work/cited_$f.txt" | tr -d ' ') tokens; those that do not resolve:"
  echo '```'; grep ': error' <<<"$out" | sed -E 's/.*error[^:]*: //' | sort | uniq | tr '\n' ' ' | fold -s -w 98; echo; echo '```'
done
echo
echo "## 8. Statement correspondence with the drafts (comment-stripped, whitespace-collapsed)"
echo
echo "\`python3 -I <OUT>/work/stmtdiff.py <draft> <proposed> [renames]\`: every declaration of the draft"
echo "against its counterpart (same name after the listed renames; names that one file qualifies and"
echo "the other opens are normalized; proofs, all \`sorry\`, removed). Docstrings are not compared."
echo
echo "### audits/evidence/stage2/Stage2Draft.lean.txt against Stage2.lean (rename startMem=initMem)"
echo '```'
(cd "$O/work" && python3 -I stmtdiff.py "$WT/audits/evidence/stage2/Stage2Draft.lean.txt" "$O/Stage2.lean" startMem=initMem) | san
echo '```'
echo
echo "### audits/evidence/stage2/ExtensionsDraft.lean.txt against LanguageExtensions.lean (rename XFits=Compiler.XFits)"
echo '```'
(cd "$O/work" && python3 -I stmtdiff.py "$WT/audits/evidence/stage2/ExtensionsDraft.lean.txt" "$O/LanguageExtensions.lean" XFits=Compiler.XFits) | san
echo '```'
echo
echo "NDSlice.lean has no draft counterpart: both of its theorems are new (NOTES.md §3.9 names the"
echo "lemma; design §15d records the need)."
} > "$LOG"
echo "wrote $LOG"

/-! ## Sanity checks of the definitions (probe only; not part of any landing module) -/

namespace WordRAM.Probe

open WordRAM

/-- Read off the emitted bits after one step. -/
def outAfter {W : ℕ} : XCfg W ⊕ Bool → List Bool
  | .inl c => c.out
  | .inr _ => []

/-- Read off a cell after one step. -/
def cellAfter {W : ℕ} (a : ℤ) : XCfg W ⊕ Bool → BitVec W
  | .inl c => c.mem a
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- Read off the position after one step. -/
def pcAfter {W : ℕ} : XCfg W ⊕ Bool → ℕ
  | .inl c => c.pc
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- Read off the coin count after one step. -/
def rdAfter {W : ℕ} : XCfg W ⊕ Bool → ℕ
  | .inl c => c.rd
  | .inr _ => 0

-- accept, reject, and reject past the end
example : xstep (W := 4) [.base .accept] [] [] (XCfg.init 4 0) = .inr true := rfl
example : xstep (W := 4) [.base .reject] [] [] (XCfg.init 4 0) = .inr false := rfl
example : xstep (W := 4) [] [] [] (XCfg.init 4 0) = .inr false := rfl
-- initMem puts |x| = 3 into cell -1; emit appends "nonzero"
example : outAfter (xstep (W := 4) [.emit (-1)] [true, false, true] [] (XCfg.init 4 3)) = [true] := by
  decide
example : outAfter (xstep (W := 4) [.emit 5] [true, false, true] [] (XCfg.init 4 3)) = [false] := by
  decide
-- rdIn: [0] := x[[-1]] = x[3]; on a 4-bit input that is the last bit
example : cellAfter 0 (xstep (W := 4) [.rdIn 0 (-1)] [false, false, false, true] []
    (XCfg.init 4 3)) = 1 := by decide
-- off the input: position 3 of a 3-bit input reads 0
example : cellAfter 0 (xstep (W := 4) [.rdIn 0 (-1)] [true, true, true] [] (XCfg.init 4 3))
    = 0 := by decide
-- a negative position reads 0: [-1] holds 15 = -1 as a signed 4-bit word
example : cellAfter 0 (xstep (W := 4) [.rdIn 0 (-1)] [true] [] (XCfg.init 4 15)) = 0 := by
  decide
-- coin reads the stream at the count, false past its end, and counts
example : cellAfter 7 (xstep (W := 4) [.coin 7] [] [true] (XCfg.init 4 0)) = 1 := by decide
example : cellAfter 7 (xstep (W := 4) [.coin 7] [] [] (XCfg.init 4 0)) = 0 := by decide
example : rdAfter (xstep (W := 4) [.coin 7] [] [] (XCfg.init 4 0)) = 1 := by decide
-- half: arithmetic shift, -3 ↦ -2 (floor) and 5 ↦ 2
example : cellAfter 0 (xstep (W := 4) [.half 0 (-1)] [] []
    { pc := 0, mem := fun a => if a = -1 then BitVec.ofInt 4 (-3) else 0, out := [], rd := 0 })
    = BitVec.ofInt 4 (-2) := by decide
example : cellAfter 0 (xstep (W := 4) [.half 0 (-1)] [] [] (XCfg.init 4 5))
    = BitVec.ofInt 4 2 := by decide
-- bltz on a negative cell jumps
example : pcAfter (xstep (W := 4) [.base (.bltz (-1) 9)] [] []
    { pc := 0, mem := fun a => if a = -1 then BitVec.ofInt 4 (-3) else 0, out := [], rd := 0 })
    = 9 := by decide
-- a straight-line base instruction goes through WordRAM.effect
example : cellAfter 2 (xstep (W := 4) [.base (.add 2 (-1) (-1))] [] [] (XCfg.init 4 3))
    = BitVec.ofInt 4 6 := by decide
-- the one-instruction accepting program halts within 1 step touching no cell
example (x ρ : List Bool) (W : ℕ) : HaltsWithin [.base .accept] x ρ W 1 true [] 0 :=
  ⟨0, XCfg.init W x.length, ∅, Nat.zero_lt_one, le_rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
-- adversarial: within one step, the rejecting program does not accept
example (x ρ : List Bool) (W f : ℕ) : ¬ HaltsWithin [.base .reject] x ρ W 1 true [] f := by
  rintro ⟨n, c, K, hn, -, hrun, hv, -⟩
  obtain rfl : n = 0 := by omega
  cases hrun
  simp [xstep] at hv
-- adversarial: nothing halts within zero steps
example (P : XProgram) (x ρ : List Bool) (W f : ℕ) (v : Bool) (o : List Bool) :
    ¬ HaltsWithin P x ρ W 0 v o f := by
  rintro ⟨n, c, K, hn, -⟩
  omega
-- the projection replaces the new instructions by reject
example : XProgram.proj [.base (.one 0), .coin 1, .base .accept] = [.one 0, .reject, .accept] :=
  rfl
-- touches: load counts the address it reads from memory
example : XInstr.touches (.base (.load 0 (-1))) (initMem 4 3) = {0, -1, 3} := by decide
-- the output modes
example : outputOf false true [false, false] = [true] := rfl
example : outputOf true true [false, false] = [false, false] := rfl
-- the bounds at a sample point: TW = 0, A = 1, n = 2, W = 3, t = 4, f = 5
example : simTime 1 (fun _ => 0) 2 3 4 5 = 5 * (5 * 4 + 9 + 2 + 1) := rfl
example : simSpace 1 (fun _ => 0) 2 3 5 = 5 * 4 + 3 + Complexity.logSpace 2 + 1 := by
  simp [simSpace]

end WordRAM.Probe

/-! ## Sanity checks of the mirror (probe only; not part of any landing module) -/

namespace Light.Probe

open Light

-- a coin then emitting it: output [true], consumed [true], cost 1 + 2
example (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (σ : State) :
    ∃ σ', XExec lim P 0 (.seq (.coin 0) (.emit (.var 0))) σ σ' [true] [true] (1 + 2) :=
  ⟨_, .seq (.coin true) (.emit trivial)⟩

-- the other coin outcome emits false
example (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (σ : State) :
    ∃ σ', XExec lim P 0 (.seq (.coin 0) (.emit (.var 0))) σ σ' [false] [false] (1 + 2) :=
  ⟨_, .seq (.coin false) (.emit trivial)⟩

-- inBit reads the input field of the limits; off the input and at negative positions it reads 0
example : inBitVal [false, true] 1 = 1 := by decide
example : inBitVal [false, true] 0 = 0 := by decide
example : inBitVal [false, true] 2 = 0 := by decide
example : inBitVal [false, true] (-1) = 0 := by decide

-- half rounds down, as WordRAM's arithmetic shift does
example : ((-3 : ℤ) / 2) = -2 := by decide
example : ((-1 : ℤ) / 2) = -1 := by decide

-- EndsIO of a coin under a stream that starts with true
example (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (σ : State) :
    EndsIO lim P 0 (.coin 3) σ [true, false] 1 fun σ' _ r => σ'.loc 3 = 1 ∧ r = [true] :=
  ⟨_, [], [true], 1, .coin true, ⟨[false], rfl⟩, le_rfl, by simp, rfl⟩

-- adversarial: under the empty stream a coin has no EndsIO run at all
example (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (σ : State) (T : ℕ) :
    ¬ EndsIO lim P 0 (.coin 3) σ [] T fun _ _ _ => True := by
  rintro ⟨σ', o, r, c, h, hr, -, -⟩
  cases h with
  | coin b => exact absurd (List.prefix_nil.mp hr) (by simp)

-- I/O-freeness: inBit and half are I/O-free, emit and coin are not
example : (XStmt.seq (.inBit 0 (.var 1)) (.half 0 (.var 0))).IOFree := ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
example : ¬ (XStmt.seq .skip (.emit (.var 0))).IOFree := fun h => h.2
example : ¬ (XStmt.while (.lt (.var 0) (.var 1)) (.coin 0)).IOFree := fun h => h

-- the conservativity map on a vendored statement
example : XStmt.ofStmt (.seq .skip (.set 0 (.const 1))) = .seq .skip (.set 0 (.const 1)) := rfl

-- the outermost statement has the text of the vendored `mainStmt` (`ProgramCode.lean:77`)
example (p0 : ℕ) : xmainStmt p0 = XStmt.ofStmt (.call p0 [.var 1, .var 2] 0) := rfl

end Light.Probe

## ===== audits/evidence/stage2-gate/upstream-Footprint.lean.txt =====

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-/
module

public import ThreeSumApsp.Machine.Steps

/-!
# What a run of the word RAM reads and writes

* One step writes at most one cell (`step_mem`) and reads at most two (`reads`, `card_reads_le`,
  `step_congr`).
* A run that ends within `t` steps changes at most `t` cells (`changed_cells`) and depends on at
  most `2t` cells (`exec_congr`); two runs from one configuration have the same result
  (`exec_unique`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ThreeSumApsp.WordRam

open EndStatement (Instr exec)

variable {W : ℕ}

/-! ## One step -/

/-- One step changes at most one cell. -/
theorem step_mem (P : List Instr) (c next : Cfg W) (h : step P c = .inl next) :
    ∃ i : ℤ, AgreeOutside {i} c.mem next.mem := by
  cases hI : P.getD c.pc .reject <;> simp only [step, hI, Sum.inl.injEq, reduceCtorEq] at h <;>
    subst h
  case bltz => exact ⟨0, fun _ _ => rfl⟩
  all_goals exact ⟨_, fun a ha => if_neg ha⟩

/-- The cells that an instruction reads. -/
def reads (m : ℤ → BitVec W) : Instr → Finset ℤ
  | .one _ => ∅
  | .add _ j k => {j, k}
  | .sub _ j k => {j, k}
  | .mul _ j k => {j, k}
  | .load _ j => {j, (m j).toInt}
  | .store i j => {i, j}
  | .bltz i _ => {i}
  | .accept => ∅
  | .reject => ∅

/-- An instruction reads at most two cells. -/
theorem card_reads_le (m : ℤ → BitVec W) (ins : Instr) : (reads m ins).card ≤ 2 := by
  cases ins <;> simp only [reads, Finset.card_empty, Finset.card_singleton] <;>
    first | omega | exact Finset.card_le_two

/-- A step from a second configuration at the same position whose memory agrees on the cells that
are read: the same verdict, or the same next position, and every cell on which the memories agreed
is a cell on which they agree afterwards. -/
theorem step_congr (P : List Instr) (c c₂ : Cfg W) (hpc : c₂.pc = c.pc)
    (hr : ∀ a ∈ reads c.mem (P.getD c.pc .reject), c₂.mem a = c.mem a) :
    (∀ v, step P c = .inr v → step P c₂ = .inr v) ∧
      ∀ next, step P c = .inl next → ∃ next₂, step P c₂ = .inl next₂ ∧ next₂.pc = next.pc ∧
        ∀ a, c₂.mem a = c.mem a → next₂.mem a = next.mem a := by
  cases hI : P.getD c.pc .reject <;> rw [hI] at hr <;>
    simp only [reads, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, forall_eq_or_imp, forall_eq,
      Finset.notMem_empty, false_imp_iff, implies_true] at hr <;>
    simp only [step, hI, hpc, Sum.inl.injEq, Sum.inr.injEq, reduceCtorEq, false_imp_iff,
      implies_true, true_and, and_true, forall_eq']
  case bltz => exact ⟨_, rfl, by simp only [hr], fun a ha => ha⟩
  all_goals exact ⟨_, rfl, rfl, fun a ha => by
    first | simp only [hr.1, hr.2] | simp only
    split_ifs <;> [rfl; exact ha]⟩

/-! ## Runs -/

/-- A run of `t` steps changes at most `t` cells. -/
theorem changed_cells (P : List Instr) : ∀ (t : ℕ) (c : Cfg W) (m' : ℤ → BitVec W) (verdict : Bool),
    exec P t c.pc c.mem = some (verdict, m') →
      ∃ S : Finset ℤ, S.card ≤ t ∧ AgreeOutside S c.mem m'
  | 0, _, _, _, h => by simp [WordRam.exec_zero] at h
  | t + 1, c, m', verdict, h => by
    cases hs : step P c with
    | inr v =>
      rw [WordRam.exec_succ_of_verdict hs] at h
      simp only [Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
      exact ⟨∅, by simp, h.2 ▸ .refl _ _⟩
    | inl n =>
      rw [WordRam.exec_succ_of_step hs] at h
      obtain ⟨S, hS, hm⟩ := changed_cells P t n m' verdict h
      obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := step_mem P c n hs
      refine ⟨insert i S, (Finset.card_insert_le _ _).trans (by omega), ?_⟩
      rw [Finset.coe_insert, Set.insert_eq]
      exact hi.trans_union hm

/-- A run of `t` steps reads at most `2t` cells: a run from the same position on a memory that
agrees on these cells gives the same verdict after the same number of steps. -/
theorem exec_congr (P : List Instr) : ∀ (t : ℕ) (c : Cfg W) (r : Bool × (ℤ → BitVec W)),
    exec P t c.pc c.mem = some r →
      ∃ R : Finset ℤ, R.card ≤ 2 * t ∧
        ∀ c₂ : Cfg W, c₂.pc = c.pc → (∀ a ∈ R, c₂.mem a = c.mem a) →
          ∃ m₂', exec P t c₂.pc c₂.mem = some (r.1, m₂')
  | 0, _, _, h => by simp [WordRam.exec_zero] at h
  | t + 1, c, r, h => by
    cases hs : step P c with
    | inr v =>
      rw [WordRam.exec_succ_of_verdict hs] at h
      refine ⟨reads c.mem (P.getD c.pc .reject), (card_reads_le _ _).trans (by omega),
        fun c₂ hpc hr => ?_⟩
      rw [WordRam.exec_succ_of_verdict ((step_congr P c c₂ hpc hr).1 v hs)]
      simp only [Option.some.injEq] at h
      exact ⟨c₂.mem, by rw [← h]⟩
    | inl n =>
      rw [WordRam.exec_succ_of_step hs] at h
      obtain ⟨R, hR, hc⟩ := exec_congr P t n r h
      have hcard := card_reads_le c.mem (P.getD c.pc .reject)
      refine ⟨reads c.mem (P.getD c.pc .reject) ∪ R,
        (Finset.card_union_le _ _).trans (by omega), fun c₂ hpc hr => ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨n₂, hs₂, hpc₂, hm₂⟩ :=
        (step_congr P c c₂ hpc fun a ha => hr a (Finset.mem_union_left _ ha)).2 n hs
      rw [WordRam.exec_succ_of_step hs₂]
      exact hc n₂ hpc₂ fun a ha => hm₂ a (hr a (Finset.mem_union_right _ ha))

/-- Two runs of a program from the same configuration have the same result. -/
theorem exec_unique {P : List Instr} {t t' : ℕ} {c : Cfg W} {r r' : Bool × (ℤ → BitVec W)}
    (h : exec P t c.pc c.mem = some r) (h' : exec P t' c.pc c.mem = some r') : r = r' := by
  have hmax := WordRam.exec_mono h (le_max_left t t')
  rw [WordRam.exec_mono h' (le_max_right t t')] at hmax
  exact (Option.some.inj hmax).symm

end ThreeSumApsp.WordRam

import TCSlib.Programs.Light.Compiler.WholeProgram
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SpaceClasses
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Constructible
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.P
import Mathlib.Data.Int.Interval

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Stage 2: the word-RAM-to-`FinTM` simulation (statement draft; PROG-4, with PROG-3)

**Status: a sorried statement draft, not for landing.** It lives in the draft namespace
`TCSlib.Draft.Stage2` and imports only modules that exist. Everything new about the RAM is
defined here by *wrapping* the vendored word RAM (`WordRAM.Instr`, `WordRAM.Cfg`,
`WordRAM.effect`), never by editing it (design §15a, §15c, §16b; backlog PROG-3, PROG-4).

A word-RAM program `P` (`XProgram`: the nine vendored instructions plus `rdIn`, `emit`, `coin`,
`half`) is run on an input `x`, a coin stream `ρ` and a word size `W`. Stage 2 says that one
`FinTM Bool` simulates it, instruction by instruction, with a polynomial time overhead and a
space bound linear in (cells touched) × (word size):

* time `TW n + A·(t + 1)·(f·(W + 1) + W² + n + 1)`, space `SW n + A·(f·(W + 1) + W + log n + 1)`,

where `n = |x|`, `t` bounds the RAM's steps, `f` the number of distinct cells it touches,
`W = W(n)` is computed by a machine within time `TW` and space `SW`, and `A` depends on `P`
only. The nondeterministic form is the same with one `FinNDTM` choice step per `coin`, under
bounds that are uniform over all coin streams.

## Deviations from the §15a draft shape (reasons in `NOTES.md`)

* **No separate address width `a`.** Addresses in this RAM are words (`load`/`store` use
  `(m j).toInt`), and the immediate addresses are constants of `P`, so a table entry has
  `W + O_P(1)` bits; `f·(W + a)` becomes `f·(W + 1)` with the constant in `A`.
* **The input seek costs `O(n + W)`, not `O(n·log n)`.** R8.5b (`Turing.exists_inputSeekTM`)
  seeks position `p` within `C·(|w| + pos + p + 1)` steps for a position word `w`; here
  `|w| ≤ W` and `pos, p ≤ n + 1`.
* **The word size enters additively.** Computing `W(n)` costs the witness's own `TW n` steps
  and `SW n` cells, once.

## Main definitions

* `XInstr`, `XProgram`, `XCfg`, `xstep`, `XSteps`: the draft extended word RAM.
* `baseTouches`, `XInstr.touches`, `XStepsIn`, `StepsIn`: cells touched along a run.
* `startMem`, `XCfg.init`, `HaltsWithin`: the start convention and the halting predicate.
* `WordSizeComputable`: the word-size hypothesis.
* `simTime`, `simSpace`, `outputOf`: the bounds and the output convention.

## Main results (all sorried)

* `exists_simulation`: stage 2, deterministic form.
* `exists_ndSimulation`: stage 2, nondeterministic form.
* `mem_DTIME_of_decides`, `mem_P_of_decides`, `mem_P_of_decides_logWord`: the P grade.
* `mem_SPACE_of_decides`, `mem_LOGSPACE_of_decides`, `computesInSpace_of_computes`,
  `mem_SPACE_mul_of_decides`: the space grades (L, log-space transducers, Savitch's shape).
* `mem_NSPACE_of_accepts`, `mem_NL_of_accepts`: the nondeterministic space grades.
* PROG-3: `StepsIn.agreeOutside`, `sim_in`, `compileProgram_footprint`,
  `haltsWithin_compileProgram`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
* [AFM26] anthropics/formal-math, folder `3sum-apsp`, commit e1a4e650, Apache-2.0: the word RAM
  and the compiler that this file wraps (vendored in `TCSlib/Programs/`).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Draft.Stage2

open WordRAM (Instr)

/-! ## The draft extended word RAM

Copied from the vendored layer: nothing is copied verbatim. `xstep` restates the match of
`WordRAM.step` (`TCSlib/Programs/WordRAM/Steps.lean:116-129`) for the nine vendored
instructions, but routes the six straight-line ones through the vendored `WordRAM.effect`
(`Steps.lean:249-257`) instead of copying their arms; `XSteps` restates `WordRAM.Steps`
(`Steps.lean:134-136`) with the input and the coin stream as parameters. -/

/-- The instructions of the draft extended word RAM: the nine instructions of the vendored
`WordRAM.Instr`, and four more. `rdIn i j` sets `[i]` to the input bit at position `[j]` (as
`0` or `1`; `0` off the input); `emit i` appends the bit "`[i]` is nonzero" to the output;
`coin i` sets `[i]` to the next coin (as `0` or `1`) and consumes it; `half i j` sets `[i]` to
`[j]` shifted right by one place, the sign kept (`⌊[j] / 2⌋`). [AFM26, `EndStatement.lean`],
extended per design §15c. -/
inductive XInstr : Type where
  | base (i : Instr)
  | rdIn (i j : ℤ)
  | emit (i : ℤ)
  | coin (i : ℤ)
  | half (i j : ℤ)

/-- A program of the draft extended word RAM: its instructions, at positions `0, 1, 2, …`. -/
abbrev XProgram : Type := List XInstr

/-- A configuration of the extended RAM: the vendored configuration (position and memory), the
bits emitted so far, and the number of coins consumed so far. The input and the coin stream are
not part of it; they are parameters of a run. -/
structure XCfg (W : ℕ) extends WordRAM.Cfg W where
  /-- The bits emitted so far, oldest first. -/
  out : List Bool
  /-- The number of coins consumed so far. -/
  rd : ℕ

/-- The word of the input bit at position `p`: `1` if `0 ≤ p` and the bit there is `true`,
`0` otherwise (in particular off the input). -/
def inBitWord (W : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (p : ℤ) : BitVec W :=
  if 0 ≤ p ∧ x.getD p.toNat false = true then 1 else 0

/-- The word of a coin: `1` for `true`, `0` for `false`. -/
def coinWord (W : ℕ) (b : Bool) : BitVec W := if b then 1 else 0

/-- One step of the extended RAM on input `x` with coin stream `ρ`: the next configuration, or
the verdict. The nine vendored instructions behave as in `WordRAM.step` and leave the output
and the coins alone; past its end the program rejects. The coin read is `ρ.getD rd false`, so a
stream that runs out reads `false`. -/
def xstep {W : ℕ} (P : XProgram) (x ρ : List Bool) (c : XCfg W) : XCfg W ⊕ Bool :=
  let m := c.mem
  match P.getD c.pc (.base .reject) with
  | .base .accept => .inr true
  | .base .reject => .inr false
  | .base (.bltz i l) => .inl { c with pc := if (m i).toInt < 0 then l else c.pc + 1 }
  | .base ins => .inl { c with pc := c.pc + 1, mem := WordRAM.effect ins m }
  | .rdIn i j =>
    .inl { c with pc := c.pc + 1, mem := Function.update m i (inBitWord W x (m j).toInt) }
  | .emit i => .inl { c with pc := c.pc + 1, out := c.out ++ [decide (m i ≠ 0)] }
  | .coin i =>
    .inl { c with pc := c.pc + 1, mem := Function.update m i (coinWord W (ρ.getD c.rd false)),
                  rd := c.rd + 1 }
  | .half i j => .inl { c with pc := c.pc + 1, mem := Function.update m i ((m j).sshiftRight 1) }

/-- `XSteps P x ρ n c c'`: exactly `n` steps of `P` on input `x` and coin stream `ρ` lead from
`c` to `c'`, none of them a verdict. The extended counterpart of `WordRAM.Steps`. -/
def XSteps {W : ℕ} (P : XProgram) (x ρ : List Bool) : ℕ → XCfg W → XCfg W → Prop
  | 0, c, c' => c = c'
  | n + 1, c, c' => ∃ c₁, xstep P x ρ c = .inl c₁ ∧ XSteps P x ρ n c₁ c'

/-- A program has no `coin` instruction. -/
def CoinFree (P : XProgram) : Prop := ∀ ins ∈ P, ∀ a : ℤ, ins ≠ .coin a

/-- The vendored program of a program of the extended RAM: the new instructions are replaced by
`reject`. A run of the vendored projection that gives no verdict executes no replaced position,
so it is also a run of the extended program (`XSteps.of_steps_proj`); this is how the vendored
run calculus and the compiler's segment lemmas are reused on code that mixes old and new
instructions. -/
def XProgram.proj (P : XProgram) : List Instr :=
  P.map fun
    | .base i => i
    | _ => .reject

section RunCalculus

variable {W : ℕ} {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool}

/-- One run after the other, as `WordRAM.Steps.trans`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the first count, as for the vendored lemma. -/
theorem XSteps.trans {n k : ℕ} {c c₁ c₂ : XCfg W} (h₁ : XSteps P x ρ n c c₁)
    (h₂ : XSteps P x ρ k c₁ c₂) : XSteps P x ρ (n + k) c c₂ := by
  sorry

/-- **Conservativity, one step.** On a program of vendored instructions, a step of the extended
RAM is the vendored step, with the output and the consumed coins unchanged.

**Proof sketch.** Both steps read `P.getD pc reject` (`List.getD_map`); case on the instruction.
The straight-line arms agree by the vendored `step_straight` computation (`1 = wd W 1`), the
branch and the verdicts literally. -/
theorem xstep_map_base (P : List Instr) (c : WordRAM.Cfg W) (o : List Bool) (r : ℕ) :
    xstep (P.map .base) x ρ ⟨c, o, r⟩ =
      Sum.map (fun c' => (⟨c', o, r⟩ : XCfg W)) id (WordRAM.step P c) := by
  sorry

/-- **Conservativity, runs.** A run of a vendored program is a run of its extended copy.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `n` with `xstep_map_base`. -/
theorem XSteps.of_steps {P : List Instr} {n : ℕ} {c c' : WordRAM.Cfg W} (h : WordRAM.Steps P n c c')
    (o : List Bool) (r : ℕ) : XSteps (P.map .base) x ρ n ⟨c, o, r⟩ ⟨c', o, r⟩ := by
  sorry

/-- **Reuse of the vendored run calculus on mixed code.** A verdict-free run of the vendored
projection `P.proj` is a run of `P` itself, with the output and the coins unchanged.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `n`. At each executed position the projection does not hold
`reject` (that would be a verdict), so `P` holds `.base` of the same instruction there, and the
step is `xstep_map_base`'s. -/
theorem XSteps.of_steps_proj {n : ℕ} {c c' : WordRAM.Cfg W} (h : WordRAM.Steps P.proj n c c')
    (o : List Bool) (r : ℕ) : XSteps P x ρ n ⟨c, o, r⟩ ⟨c', o, r⟩ := by
  sorry

end RunCalculus

/-! ## Cells touched along a run (PROG-3 at the RAM level) -/

/-- The cells that a vendored instruction reads or writes in the memory `m`: its named cells,
and for `load`/`store` also the cell whose address it reads from memory. -/
def baseTouches {W : ℕ} (ins : Instr) (m : ℤ → BitVec W) : Finset ℤ :=
  match ins with
  | .one i => {i}
  | .add i j k => {i, j, k}
  | .sub i j k => {i, j, k}
  | .mul i j k => {i, j, k}
  | .load i j => {i, j, (m j).toInt}
  | .store i j => {i, j, (m i).toInt}
  | .bltz i _ => {i}
  | .accept => ∅
  | .reject => ∅

/-- The cells that an instruction of the extended RAM reads or writes in the memory `m`. -/
def XInstr.touches {W : ℕ} : XInstr → (ℤ → BitVec W) → Finset ℤ
  | .base ins, m => baseTouches ins m
  | .rdIn i j, _ => {i, j}
  | .emit i, _ => {i}
  | .coin i, _ => {i}
  | .half i j, _ => {i, j}

/-- `XStepsIn P x ρ K n c c'`: an `XSteps` run in which every step reads and writes only cells
of `K`. Every run is an `XStepsIn` run for the set of the cells it touches; `K` is the
footprint. -/
def XStepsIn {W : ℕ} (P : XProgram) (x ρ : List Bool) (K : Set ℤ) :
    ℕ → XCfg W → XCfg W → Prop
  | 0, c, c' => c = c'
  | n + 1, c, c' => ∃ c₁, xstep P x ρ c = .inl c₁ ∧
      ↑((P.getD c.pc (.base .reject)).touches c.mem) ⊆ K ∧ XStepsIn P x ρ K n c₁ c'

/-- `StepsIn P K n c c'`: a `WordRAM.Steps` run of a vendored program in which every step reads
and writes only cells of `K`. The PROG-3 strengthening of `WordRAM.Steps`, added beside it (the
vendored definition is not changed). -/
def StepsIn {W : ℕ} (P : List Instr) (K : Set ℤ) : ℕ → WordRAM.Cfg W → WordRAM.Cfg W → Prop
  | 0, c, c' => c = c'
  | n + 1, c, c' => ∃ c₁, WordRAM.step P c = .inl c₁ ∧
      ↑(baseTouches (P.getD c.pc .reject) c.mem) ⊆ K ∧ StepsIn P K n c₁ c'

section Footprints

variable {W : ℕ} {K K' : Set ℤ}

/-- A run within a footprint is a run of `WordRAM.Steps`, the footprint forgotten. -/
theorem StepsIn.toSteps {P : List Instr} {n : ℕ} {c c' : WordRAM.Cfg W} (h : StepsIn P K n c c') :
    WordRAM.Steps P n c c' := by
  sorry

/-- Every run has a footprint: the cells it touches. (So `StepsIn` loses nothing.)

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `n`; take the union of the first step's touched cells and the
footprint of the rest. -/
theorem Steps.exists_stepsIn {P : List Instr} {n : ℕ} {c c' : WordRAM.Cfg W}
    (h : WordRAM.Steps P n c c') : ∃ K : Finset ℤ, StepsIn P (↑K) n c c' := by
  sorry

/-- A run within a footprint is a run within every larger set of cells. -/
theorem StepsIn.mono {P : List Instr} {n : ℕ} {c c' : WordRAM.Cfg W} (h : StepsIn P K n c c')
    (hK : K ⊆ K') : StepsIn P K' n c c' := by
  sorry

/-- One run after the other, within the union of the footprints. -/
theorem StepsIn.trans {P : List Instr} {n k : ℕ} {c c₁ c₂ : WordRAM.Cfg W}
    (h₁ : StepsIn P K n c c₁) (h₂ : StepsIn P K' k c₁ c₂) : StepsIn P (K ∪ K') (n + k) c c₂ := by
  sorry

/-- **Every intermediate memory stays inside the footprint.** Along a run within `K`, every
configuration reached after `k ≤ n` steps has a memory that agrees with the starting memory
outside `K`, and the rest of the run is again within `K`. (The obstacle 1 of design §15c: the
vendored `Finished` and `compileProgram_correct` speak of the last memory only.)

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `k`. A step writes only its target cell, which is among the cells
it touches (`baseTouches` lists the target of each writing instruction, `(m i).toInt` for
`store`), so the memory after the step agrees with the one before outside `K`
(`WordRAM.AgreeOutside.update`). -/
theorem StepsIn.agreeOutside {P : List Instr} {n : ℕ} {c c' : WordRAM.Cfg W}
    (h : StepsIn P K n c c') {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n) :
    ∃ d : WordRAM.Cfg W, StepsIn P K k c d ∧ StepsIn P K (n - k) d c' ∧
      WordRAM.AgreeOutside K c.mem d.mem := by
  sorry

/-- The straight-line row with its footprint: a list of vendored instructions without `load`
and `store` touches only the cells it names. (`load` and `store` need the known-number rows
`steps_load`/`steps_store` with the address added to the footprint.)

**Proof sketch.** As `WordRAM.steps_straight`, collecting `baseTouches` of each instruction. -/
theorem stepsIn_straight {P : List Instr} (l : List Instr) (pc : ℕ) (m : ℤ → BitVec W)
    (hcode : WordRAM.CodeAt P pc l) (hl : ∀ i ∈ l, WordRAM.Straight i)
    (hK : ∀ i ∈ l, ∀ m' : ℤ → BitVec W, ↑(baseTouches i m') ⊆ K) :
    StepsIn P K l.length ⟨pc, m⟩ ⟨pc + l.length, WordRAM.effects l m⟩ := by
  sorry

/-- An extended run within a footprint is an `XSteps` run, the footprint forgotten. -/
theorem XStepsIn.toXSteps {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool} {n : ℕ} {c c' : XCfg W}
    (h : XStepsIn P x ρ K n c c') : XSteps P x ρ n c c' := by
  sorry

/-- Every extended run has a footprint: the finite set of the cells it touches. -/
theorem XSteps.exists_xStepsIn {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool} {n : ℕ} {c c' : XCfg W}
    (h : XSteps P x ρ n c c') : ∃ K : Finset ℤ, XStepsIn P x ρ (↑K) n c c' := by
  sorry

/-- The footprint version of `XSteps.of_steps_proj`: a verdict-free run of the projection within
`K` is a run of the extended program within `K`. -/
theorem XStepsIn.of_stepsIn_proj {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool} {n : ℕ}
    {c c' : WordRAM.Cfg W} (h : StepsIn P.proj K n c c') (o : List Bool) (r : ℕ) :
    XStepsIn P x ρ K n ⟨c, o, r⟩ ⟨c', o, r⟩ := by
  sorry

end Footprints

/-! ## Starting, halting -/

/-- The memory in which stage 2 starts a RAM program on an input of length `n`: the cell `-1`
(the compiler's argument cell `Light.Compiler.cARG1`) holds `n`, every other cell `0`. So a
compiled program receives `|x|` as its first argument (design §15c: `inLen` from an argument
cell). -/
def startMem (W n : ℕ) : ℤ → BitVec W :=
  Function.update (fun _ => 0) Light.Compiler.cARG1 (WordRAM.wd W n)

/-- The start configuration on an input of length `n`: position `0`, `startMem`, nothing
emitted, no coin consumed. -/
def XCfg.init (W n : ℕ) : XCfg W := { pc := 0, mem := startMem W n, out := [], rd := 0 }

/-- `HaltsWithin P x ρ W t v o f`: run on the input `x` with the coin stream `ρ` and word size
`W`, the program `P` gives the verdict `v` within `t` steps (the verdict step counted, as in
`WordRAM.exec`), has then emitted `o`, and has touched at most `f` distinct cells. -/
def HaltsWithin (P : XProgram) (x ρ : List Bool) (W t : ℕ) (v : Bool) (o : List Bool) (f : ℕ) :
    Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (c : XCfg W) (K : Finset ℤ), n < t ∧ K.card ≤ f ∧
    XStepsIn P x ρ (↑K) n (XCfg.init W x.length) c ∧ xstep P x ρ c = .inr v ∧ c.out = o

section Halting

variable {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool} {W t t' f f' : ℕ} {v v' : Bool} {o o' : List Bool}

/-- A run that halts within `t` steps and `f` cells halts within any larger bounds. -/
theorem HaltsWithin.mono (h : HaltsWithin P x ρ W t v o f) (ht : t ≤ t') (hf : f ≤ f') :
    HaltsWithin P x ρ W t' v o f' := by
  sorry

/-- The run is determined by the input, the coin stream and the word size: two halting runs have
the same verdict and output.

**Proof sketch.** `xstep` is a function, so the two `XSteps` runs agree up to the shorter
length, where one of them gives a verdict; a run that gives no verdict cannot continue past a
verdict, so the lengths agree. -/
theorem HaltsWithin.unique (h : HaltsWithin P x ρ W t v o f)
    (h' : HaltsWithin P x ρ W t' v' o' f') :
    v = v' ∧ o = o' := by
  sorry

/-- A program without `coin` does not depend on the coin stream.

**Proof sketch.** `xstep` reads `ρ` only at a `coin` instruction; induction on the run. -/
theorem HaltsWithin.coin_irrel (hP : CoinFree P) (ρ' : List Bool) :
    HaltsWithin P x ρ W t v o f ↔ HaltsWithin P x ρ' W t v o f := by
  sorry

end Halting

/-! ## The word size -/

/-- **The word size is computable.** Some machine outputs the binary representation of
`W (|x|)` (`Nat.bits`, as in `Complexity.SpaceConstructible`) from `x` within `TW |x|` steps,
visiting at most `SW |x|` work cells. The stage-2 machine runs it once, at the start, with its
output redirected to a work tape (the R1 embedding), and pays `TW` and `SW` once. (Design §16b
item 1: `W = c·log n` for P and L, `W = c·S(n)` for Savitch.) -/
def WordSizeComputable (W TW SW : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ M : Turing.FinTM Bool, ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t ≤ TW x.length,
    M.ComputesInTime x (W x.length).bits t ∧ M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ SW x.length

/-- A word size computable within `TW` and `SW` is computable within any larger bounds. -/
theorem WordSizeComputable.mono {W TW SW TW' SW' : ℕ → ℕ} (h : WordSizeComputable W TW SW)
    (hT : ∀ n, TW n ≤ TW' n) (hS : ∀ n, SW n ≤ SW' n) : WordSizeComputable W TW' SW' := by
  sorry

/-- **Logarithmic word sizes** (P and L): for every `c`, the word size `c·(⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)` is
computable in linear time and logarithmic space.

**Proof sketch.** R8.5c (`Turing.exists_inputLengthTM`) writes `Nat.bits |x|` on a work tape
within `C·(|x| + 1)` steps and `C·(|bits |x|| + 1)` cells. Its length is `logSpace |x|` for
`|x| ≠ 0` (the private `b3a_bits_length`, `Constructible.lean:66`, to be promoted) and is
fixed up at `|x| = 0`; a counter
pass over the word writes that length in binary, and a carry pass multiplies it by `c`. -/
theorem wordSizeComputable_logSpace (c : ℕ) :
    ∃ a : ℕ, WordSizeComputable (fun n => c * Complexity.logSpace n) (fun n => a * (n + 1))
      (fun n => a * Complexity.logSpace n) := by
  sorry

/-- **Space-constructible word sizes** (Savitch): if `S` is space-constructible, then for
every `c` the word size `c·S(n)` is computable in space `O(S(n))`, within some time bound (not
controlled, and not needed by the space grades).

**Proof sketch.** Run the constructibility witness and multiply its binary output by `c` (a
carry pass). It halts on every input, so the largest halting time over the finitely many inputs
of each length is a time bound `TW`. -/
theorem wordSizeComputable_of_spaceConstructible {S : ℕ → ℕ} (hS : Complexity.SpaceConstructible S)
    (c : ℕ) :
    ∃ (a : ℕ) (TW : ℕ → ℕ), WordSizeComputable (fun n => c * S n) TW (fun n => a * S n) := by
  sorry

/-! ## Stage 2 -/

/-- The time bound of stage 2: computing the word size, then `t + 1` simulated steps, each at
most one scan of a table of `f` entries of `W + O(1)` bits, one shift-and-add multiplication,
and one input seek. -/
def simTime (A : ℕ) (TW : ℕ → ℕ) (n W t f : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  TW n + A * (t + 1) * (f * (W + 1) + W ^ 2 + n + 1)

/-- The space bound of stage 2: computing the word size, then the memory table (`f` entries),
`O(1)` words of scratch, and the input length. -/
def simSpace (A : ℕ) (SW : ℕ → ℕ) (n W f : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  SW n + A * (f * (W + 1) + W + Complexity.logSpace n + 1)

/-- What the stage-2 machine leaves on its output tape: in verdict mode (`fn = false`) the
one-bit verdict, as `Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime` reads it; in function mode (`fn = true`) the
emitted word, as `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace` reads it. -/
def outputOf (fn v : Bool) (o : List Bool) : List Bool := if fn then o else [v]

/-- **Stage 2, deterministic form** (design §15a, §16b; backlog PROG-4). For every program `P`
of the extended word RAM, every output mode and every computable word size `W`, there are a
machine `M` and a constant `A` such that: whenever `P`, run on `x` with word size `W(|x|)` (and
the empty coin stream: coins read `0`), gives the verdict `v` within `t` steps, having emitted
`o` and touched at most `f` cells, `M` halts on `x` within
`TW n + A·(t + 1)·(f·(W + 1) + W² + n + 1)` steps with `outputOf fn v o` on its output tape,
having visited at most `SW n + A·(f·(W + 1) + W + log n + 1)` work cells (`n = |x|`).
[AB09, Exercise 1.9: a machine with random access memory is simulated with polynomial overhead]

Deviations: [AB09] has a bit-array RAM and the bound `T(n)²`; this is [AFM26]'s word RAM with
input, output and coins, and an explicit bound in steps, cells and word size. From the §15a draft:
no separate address width, an `n` (not `n·log n`) seek term, and the word size's own cost added
(module docstring).

**Proof sketch.** The machine is a phase host over the positions of `P` (finitely many, since
`P` is fixed), after a start-up.
1. *Start-up.* Run the word-size witness with its output on a work tape (R1 embedding), turn it
   into a unary ruler of `W` cells; count `|x|` (R8.5c) and install the table entry
   `-1 ↦ |x| mod 2^W`. Cost `TW n + O(n + W²)`, space `SW n + O(W + log n)`.
2. *One phase per position.* Each instruction kind is a `Turing.Contract` (MIG-0a) whose
   precondition says that the tapes encode a RAM configuration (a memory table of
   (address, word) pairs, a program-counter phase, the ruler, the input length) and whose
   endpoint encodes its `xstep`: find-by-key in the table (the new row of §15a), two-tape
   addition/subtraction modulo `2^W`, shift-and-add multiplication, the sign test (`bltz`), the
   arithmetic shift (`half`), table overwrite or append, the input seek R8.5b (`rdIn`, after a
   range test against `|x|`), an output append (`emit`, function mode only). `coin` writes `0`.
   Each costs at most `A·(f·(W + 1) + W² + n + 1)` steps on a table of at most `f + 1` entries.
3. *Simulation.* Induction on the `XStepsIn` run: the encoding invariant holds after every
   step, and the table holds only cells of the footprint `K` (and `-1`), so it never exceeds
   `|K| + 1 ≤ f + 1` entries of `W + O_P(1)` bits.
4. *Verdict.* At `accept`/`reject`, write `[v]` in verdict mode, and halt. -/
theorem exists_simulation (P : XProgram) (fn : Bool) {W TW SW : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hW : WordSizeComputable W TW SW) :
    ∃ (M : Turing.FinTM Bool) (A : ℕ), ∀ (x : List Bool) (t f : ℕ) (v : Bool) (o : List Bool),
      HaltsWithin P x [] (W x.length) t v o f →
        M.ComputesInTime x (outputOf fn v o) (simTime A TW x.length (W x.length) t f) ∧
        M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) (simTime A TW x.length (W x.length) t f) ≤
          simSpace A SW x.length (W x.length) f := by
  sorry

/-- **Stage 2, nondeterministic form** (design §15c, §16b item 4; backlog PROG-4). For every
program `P` of the extended word RAM and every computable word size `W` there are a
nondeterministic machine `N` and a constant `A` such that: if, on the input `x`, **every** coin
stream lets `P` give a verdict within `t` steps touching at most `f` cells (bounds uniform over
the streams, as `NTIME` and `NSPACE` require), then every branch of `N` of length
`T = simTime …` has halted, every such branch has visited at most `simSpace …` work cells, and
`N` accepts `x` within `T` exactly when some coin stream makes `P` accept.
[AB09, Exercise 1.9 with §2.1.2 (NDTMs) and Def 4.1 (nondeterministic space)]

**Proof sketch.** As `exists_simulation`, in verdict mode, with one change: the phase for
`coin i` is a single choice step whose two transitions write `0` or `1` into the table entry of
`i`; every other step ignores its choice bit (its two transitions coincide). A branch, a choice
word `w` of length `T`, then simulates the RAM run whose coin stream is the subsequence of `w`
at the coin steps; conversely every coin stream is realized by a branch that places its bits
there. All branches are runs of `P` on some stream, so the uniform bounds bound every branch. -/
theorem exists_ndSimulation (P : XProgram) {W TW SW : ℕ → ℕ} (hW : WordSizeComputable W TW SW) :
    ∃ (N : Turing.FinNDTM Bool) (A : ℕ), ∀ (x : List Bool) (t f : ℕ),
      (∀ ρ : List Bool, ∃ (v : Bool) (o : List Bool), HaltsWithin P x ρ (W x.length) t v o f) →
        N.tm.HaltsWithin x (simTime A TW x.length (W x.length) t f) ∧
        (∀ w : List Bool, w.length = simTime A TW x.length (W x.length) t f →
          N.tm.spaceUsedWith w (N.tm.initCfg x) ≤ simSpace A SW x.length (W x.length) f) ∧
        (N.AcceptsWithin x (simTime A TW x.length (W x.length) t f) ↔
          ∃ (ρ o : List Bool), HaltsWithin P x ρ (W x.length) t true o f) := by
  sorry

/-! ## The time grade: P -/

/-- **Deciding in time.** If `P` decides `L` (verdict `[x ∈ L]`) with word size `W`, within `T`
steps and `F` cells, then `L ∈ DTIME T'` for every `T'` that dominates the stage-2 time bound
up to a constant. [AB09, Def 1.12]

**Proof sketch.** `exists_simulation` in verdict mode; `ComputesInTime.mono` moves each input's
time to `a · T' |x|` (`simTime` is monotone in `t` and `f`). -/
theorem mem_DTIME_of_decides (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) {W TW SW T F : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hW : WordSizeComputable W TW SW)
    (hdec : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ o : List Bool,
      HaltsWithin P x [] (W x.length) (T x.length)
        (Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x) o (F x.length))
    (T' : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ)
    (hT : ∀ n, TW n + (T n + 1) * (F n * (W n + 1) + W n ^ 2 + n + 1) ≤ a * T' n) :
    L ∈ Complexity.DTIME T' := by
  sorry

/-- **The P grade.** If `P` decides `L` with polynomially many steps and cells and a word size
of polynomial value that is computable in polynomial time, then `L ∈ P`. [AB09, Def 1.13]

**Proof sketch.** `mem_DTIME_of_decides` with `T' n = (n + 1)^d'` for `d'` large
(`(t + 1)·(f·(W + 1) + W² + n + 1)` is a polynomial of polynomials), then
`Complexity.mem_P_iff`. -/
theorem mem_P_of_decides (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) {W TW SW : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hW : WordSizeComputable W TW SW) (C d : ℕ)
    (hWpoly : ∀ n, TW n + W n ≤ C * (n + 1) ^ d)
    (hdec : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ (t f : ℕ) (o : List Bool),
      t ≤ C * (x.length + 1) ^ d ∧ f ≤ C * (x.length + 1) ^ d ∧
      HaltsWithin P x [] (W x.length) t
        (Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x) o f) :
    L ∈ Complexity.P := by
  sorry

/-- **The P grade with logarithmic words**, the form the curriculum and `NL ⊆ P` use: word size
`c·(⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)`, polynomially many steps and cells.

**Proof sketch.** `mem_P_of_decides` with `wordSizeComputable_logSpace c`; `logSpace n ≤ n + 1`. -/
theorem mem_P_of_decides_logWord (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) (c C d : ℕ)
    (hdec : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ (t f : ℕ) (o : List Bool),
      t ≤ C * (x.length + 1) ^ d ∧ f ≤ C * (x.length + 1) ^ d ∧
      HaltsWithin P x [] (c * Complexity.logSpace x.length) t
        (Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x) o f) :
    L ∈ Complexity.P := by
  sorry

/-! ## The space grades: L, log-space transducers, Savitch's shape -/

/-- **Deciding in space.** If `P` decides `L` with word size `W` touching at most `F` cells (in
any number of steps), then `L ∈ SPACE s` for every `s` that dominates
`SW + F·(W + 1) + W + log n + 1` up to a constant. [AB09, Def 4.1]

**Proof sketch.** `exists_simulation` in verdict mode gives, on each input, a halting time and
the space bound `simSpace A SW n W (F n) ≤ A·(…) ≤ A·a·s n`. -/
theorem mem_SPACE_of_decides (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) {W TW SW F : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hW : WordSizeComputable W TW SW)
    (hdec : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ (t : ℕ) (o : List Bool),
      HaltsWithin P x [] (W x.length) t (Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x) o
        (F x.length))
    (s : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ)
    (hs : ∀ n, SW n + F n * (W n + 1) + W n + Complexity.logSpace n + 1 ≤ a * s n) :
    L ∈ Complexity.SPACE s := by
  sorry

/-- **The logspace grade** (design §15a, §16b item 4): a program that decides `L` touching
`O(1)` cells with word size `c·(⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)` puts `L` in `L`. The input is read in place
(`rdIn`), so it costs no cells. [AB09, Def 4.5]

**Proof sketch.** `mem_SPACE_of_decides` with `wordSizeComputable_logSpace c`, `F = F₀` and
`s = logSpace`: `a·logSpace n + F₀·(c·logSpace n + 1) + c·logSpace n + logSpace n + 1` is at most
a constant times `logSpace n`, since `logSpace n ≥ 1`. -/
theorem mem_LOGSPACE_of_decides (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) (c F₀ : ℕ)
    (hdec : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ (t : ℕ) (o : List Bool),
      HaltsWithin P x [] (c * Complexity.logSpace x.length) t
        (Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x) o F₀) :
    L ∈ Complexity.LOGSPACE := by
  sorry

/-- **Log-space transducers**: a program that, on every `x`, emits `g x` touching `O(1)` cells
with word size `c·(⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)` gives a machine computing `g` in logarithmic space (the
output tape is append-only and not counted). [AB09, §4.3, log-space reductions]

**Proof sketch.** `exists_simulation` in function mode, with the bounds of
`mem_LOGSPACE_of_decides`. -/
theorem computesInSpace_of_computes (P : XProgram) (g : List Bool → List Bool) (c F₀ : ℕ)
    (hcomp : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ (t : ℕ) (v : Bool),
      HaltsWithin P x [] (c * Complexity.logSpace x.length) t v (g x) F₀) :
    ∃ (M : Turing.FinTM Bool) (a : ℕ), M.ComputesInSpace g fun n => a * Complexity.logSpace n := by
  sorry

/-- **Savitch's shape** (design §16b item 1): with a space-constructible `S`, word size `c·S(n)`
and at most `c·S(n)` cells (depth `O(S)` frames of `O(1)` words), `L ∈ SPACE(S²)`.
[AB09, Theorem 4.14's space accounting]

**Proof sketch.** `mem_SPACE_of_decides` with `wordSizeComputable_of_spaceConstructible hS c`:
`a·S + c·S·(c·S + 1) + c·S + logSpace + 1 ≤ a'·S²`, since `logSpace ≤ S` (a conjunct of
`SpaceConstructible`) and so `S ≥ 1`. -/
theorem mem_SPACE_mul_of_decides (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) {S : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hS : Complexity.SpaceConstructible S) (c : ℕ)
    (hdec : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ (t : ℕ) (o : List Bool),
      HaltsWithin P x [] (c * S x.length) t (Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x) o
        (c * S x.length)) :
    L ∈ Complexity.SPACE fun n => S n * S n := by
  sorry

/-! ## The nondeterministic space grades: NL -/

/-- **Accepting in nondeterministic space.** If, on every `x`, every coin stream lets `P` halt
within some uniform `t` touching at most `F |x|` cells with word size `W`, and `x ∈ L` exactly
when some stream makes `P` accept, then `L ∈ NSPACE s` for every `s` that dominates the
stage-2 space bound up to a constant. [AB09, Def 4.1, nondeterministic clause]

**Proof sketch.** `exists_ndSimulation`; the budget of `Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace` is
`simTime A TW n W t f`, all branches halt and stay within `simSpace …`, and acceptance is the
stated equivalence. -/
theorem mem_NSPACE_of_accepts (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) {W TW SW F : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hW : WordSizeComputable W TW SW)
    (hrun : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t : ℕ,
      (∀ ρ : List Bool, ∃ (v : Bool) (o : List Bool),
        HaltsWithin P x ρ (W x.length) t v o (F x.length)) ∧
      (x ∈ L ↔ ∃ (ρ o : List Bool), HaltsWithin P x ρ (W x.length) t true o (F x.length)))
    (s : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ)
    (hs : ∀ n, SW n + F n * (W n + 1) + W n + Complexity.logSpace n + 1 ≤ a * s n) :
    L ∈ Complexity.NSPACE s := by
  sorry

/-- **The NL grade** (design §16b item 4, C2): a program with read-once coins that, on every
`x`, halts under every coin stream within a uniform time touching `O(1)` cells with word size
`c·(⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)`, and accepts under some stream exactly when `x ∈ L`, puts `L` in `NL`.
[AB09, Def 4.5 (NL), Def 4.1]

**Proof sketch.** `mem_NSPACE_of_accepts` with `wordSizeComputable_logSpace c`, `F = F₀`,
`s = logSpace`, as in `mem_LOGSPACE_of_decides`. -/
theorem mem_NL_of_accepts (P : XProgram) (L : Language Bool) (c F₀ : ℕ)
    (hrun : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t : ℕ,
      (∀ ρ : List Bool, ∃ (v : Bool) (o : List Bool),
        HaltsWithin P x ρ (c * Complexity.logSpace x.length) t v o F₀) ∧
      (x ∈ L ↔ ∃ (ρ o : List Bool),
        HaltsWithin P x ρ (c * Complexity.logSpace x.length) t true o F₀)) :
    L ∈ Complexity.NL := by
  sorry

/-! ## PROG-3 at the compiler level: the footprint of compiled code

The vendored simulation (`Light.Compiler.sim`, `Simulation.lean:284`) produces
`Finished.run : Steps S.code n ⟨pos, m⟩ ⟨pos + s.size S.F, m'⟩` and the frame
`Finished.agree : AgreeOutside (Writable S.toSizes q) m m'`, which speaks of the last memory
only. The strengthening adds the footprint of the run itself. -/

section Compiled

open Light Light.Compiler

variable {W : ℕ}

/-- The cells that the code of a statement running in the frame `q` may read or write: those it
may write (`Light.Compiler.Writable`: scratch, `FP`, the stack from `q` on, the light memory
within the limits) and the constants it reads (`1`, `0`, `-1` and the pool). -/
def Touchable (Z : Sizes W) (q : ℕ) : Set ℤ := Writable Z q ∪ Constants Z.disp

/-- `Light.Compiler.Finished` with the footprint of the run: the same run, within the cells
that a statement in the frame `q` may touch. -/
structure FinishedIn (S : Setting W) (s : Stmt) (σ' : State) (c pos q : ℕ) (m m' : ℤ → BitVec W)
    (n : ℕ) : Prop extends Finished S s σ' c pos q m m' n where
  /-- The run touches only cells that the statement may touch. -/
  runIn : StepsIn S.code (Touchable S.toSizes q) n ⟨pos, m⟩ ⟨pos + s.size S.F, m'⟩

/-- **The simulation theorem with footprints** (PROG-3). The code of a statement matches every
run of the statement, and the matching run of the machine touches only cells that a statement
in its frame may touch. Strengthens `Light.Compiler.sim`.

**Proof sketch.** The induction of `sim`, case by case (`sim_skip`, …, `sim_call`), carrying
`StepsIn` through `StepsIn.trans`. The segment lemmas need footprint twins: straight-line code
(`stepsIn_straight`), the jump, the dispatcher, the test code, the argument and frame code, and
the loads and stores, whose addresses are known numbers: a local variable's cell
`cStack (q + x)` with `x < F` (in `Stack q Q`), a light address within `lim.space` (`Safe`),
or the return position `cStack (q + F)`. A call's body runs in the frame `q + F + 1`, whose
touchable cells lie in those of `q` (`writable_subset_writable`). -/
theorem sim_in (S : Setting W) {d : ℕ} {s : Stmt} {σ σ' : State} {c : ℕ}
    (h : Exec S.lim S.P d s σ σ' c) (pos q : ℕ) (m : ℤ → BitVec W) (B : Start S d s σ pos q m) :
    ∃ (m' : ℤ → BitVec W) (n : ℕ), FinishedIn S s σ' c pos q m m' n := by
  sorry

/-- The region of a compiled program: the cells from `-lowCell` up to (not including)
`lim.space`. `Light.Compiler.Outcome.far` says that the cells outside it are unchanged at the
end; `compileProgram_footprint` says that no step touches them. -/
def region (P : Program) (dec : Bool) (lim : Limits) : Finset ℤ :=
  Finset.Ico (-(lowCell P dec lim : ℤ)) (lim.space : ℤ)

/-- The region has `lowCell + lim.space` cells.

**Proof sketch.** `Int.card_Ico`. -/
theorem card_region (P : Program) (dec : Bool) (lim : Limits) :
    (region P dec lim).card = lowCell P dec lim + lim.space := by
  sorry

/-- **The compiled program stays in its region** (PROG-3, design §15c obstacle 1). Under the
hypotheses of `Light.compileProgram_correct`, the compiled program gives its verdict within
`ramSteps P dec c` steps by a run that touches no cell outside `[-lowCell, lim.space)`, and it
ends as `Outcome` says. Strengthens `compileProgram_correct` from the final memory to every
intermediate one (with `StepsIn.agreeOutside`).

**Proof sketch.** As `compileProgram_correct`, with `sim_in` in place of `sim`: the start-up
code (straight-line, cells `Constants ∪ {FP} ∪ MainFrame` and the argument cells `-1`, `-2`), the
outermost statement (`Touchable` of `mainFrame`), and the verdict code (`cRESULT`, `D`,
`cStack mainFrame`, `ZERO`) all lie in the region (the cell computations of `not_mem_of_far`,
now for reads as well as writes). -/
theorem compileProgram_footprint {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {p0 : ℕ} {dec : Bool} {μ : ℕ → ℤ}
    {i j : ℤ} {σ' : State} {c : ℕ} {m : ℤ → BitVec W}
    (h : Exec lim P 0 (mainStmt p0) ⟨frame [0, i, j], μ⟩ σ' c)
    (hfit : Fits W lim (dispPos P dec) (stackCells P lim)) (hm : Input lim μ i j m) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (cfg : WordRAM.Cfg W), n < ramSteps P dec c ∧
      StepsIn (compileProgram P p0 dec) ↑(region P dec lim) n ⟨0, m⟩ cfg ∧
      WordRAM.step (compileProgram P p0 dec) cfg = .inr (verdictOf dec (σ'.loc 0)) ∧
      Outcome lim P dec m σ' cfg.mem := by
  sorry

/-- **The interface between stage 1 and stage 2**, for the vendored compiler (no input access,
so only the length of the input is available, as the first argument). A light run of the
outermost call on `(|x|, 0)` from the empty memory gives stage 2's hypothesis for the compiled
program: the same verdict within `ramSteps` steps, touching at most `lowCell + lim.space`
cells. With the extended compiler (PROG-2) the same statement reads the input through `inBit`.

**Proof sketch.** `startMem W |x|` satisfies `Input lim 0 |x| 0` (`cARG1 = -1`; every other
cell, `-2` included, holds `0`). `compileProgram_footprint` gives the run within the region;
`XStepsIn.of_stepsIn_proj` (the projection of `(compileProgram …).map .base` is
`compileProgram …`) lifts it, `xstep_map_base` lifts the verdict step, and `card_region`
counts the cells. -/
theorem haltsWithin_compileProgram {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {p0 : ℕ} {dec : Bool} {σ' : State}
    {c : ℕ} (x ρ : List Bool)
    (h : Exec lim P 0 (mainStmt p0) ⟨frame [0, (x.length : ℤ), 0], fun _ => 0⟩ σ' c)
    (hfit : Fits W lim (dispPos P dec) (stackCells P lim)) (hn : (x.length : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) :
    HaltsWithin ((compileProgram P p0 dec).map .base) x ρ W (ramSteps P dec c)
      (verdictOf dec (σ'.loc 0)) [] (lowCell P dec lim + lim.space) := by
  sorry

end Compiled

end TCSlib.Draft.Stage2

/-

import TCSlib.Programs.Light.Assigns
import TCSlib.Programs.Light.Calls
import TCSlib.Programs.Light.RunsStayInLimits
import TCSlib.Programs.Light.Compiler.Cells
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Classes

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The language extensions: signatures (statement draft; PROG-2)

**Status: a sorried, self-contained mirror, not for landing.** The real edit set changes the
vendored `Light.Stmt`, `Light.Exec`, `Light.Limits`, `Light.Ends` and `Light.Compiler.Fits` in
place (design §15c; backlog PROG-2). Because a draft cannot change compiled modules, this file
mirrors them in the namespace `TCSlib.Draft.Stage2.Lang` under the names `XStmt`, `XExec`,
`XLimits`, `XEnds` and `XFits`, and states the new rules and lemmas over the mirror.

## What is copied

* `XStmt` copies the seven constructors of `Light.Stmt` (`Syntax.lean:80-88`) and adds four.
* `XExec` copies the nine rules of `Light.Exec` (`Syntax.lean:155-174`), adding the indices `o`
  (bits emitted) and `r` (coins consumed), concatenated by `seq` and `whileTrue` and passed
  through `call`; it adds four rules.
* `XEnds` copies `Light.Ends` (`Logic.lean:78-80`) with the two indices under `∃`.
* `XStmt.assigns` copies `Light.Stmt.assigns` (`Assigns.lean:43-51`) and adds four cases.
* Expressions, tests, states, `frame`, `Expr.Safe` and the cost functions are the vendored ones,
  unchanged: the new constructs are statements, because expression code must be `Straight` and
  `effect` touches only memory (design §15c).

## The semantics (design §15c)

* `x := inBit e`: the input bit at position `e` as `0`/`1`, `0` off the input; cost `e.cost + 1`.
  The input is a field of the limits. `inLen` is not a construct: `|x|` comes as an argument.
* `emit e`: appends the bit "`e` is nonzero"; cost `e.cost + 1`.
* `x := coin`: either bit, consumed; cost `1`. A fixed stream `ρ` selects the run whose consumed
  word is a prefix of `ρ` (`EndsIO`); that run is unique (`XExec.det`).
* `x := half e`: `⌊e / 2⌋`; cost `e.cost + 1`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
* [AFM26] anthropics/formal-math, folder `3sum-apsp`, commit e1a4e650, Apache-2.0: the light
  language and its logic (vendored in `TCSlib/Programs/Light/`), of which this is an extension.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Draft.Stage2.Lang

open Light (Op Expr Cond State Limits frame)

/-- Statements of the extended light language: the seven of `Light.Stmt`, and `x := inBit e`
(the input bit at position `e`), `emit e` (append the bit "`e ≠ 0`" to the output), `x := coin`
(the next coin), `x := half e` (`⌊e / 2⌋`). [AFM26, `Lang/Syntax.lean`], extended per design
§15c. -/
inductive XStmt : Type
  | skip
  | set (x : ℕ) (e : Expr)
  | store (a e : Expr)
  | seq (s₁ s₂ : XStmt)
  | ite (c : Cond) (s₁ s₂ : XStmt)
  | while (c : Cond) (s : XStmt)
  | call (p : ℕ) (args : List Expr) (x : ℕ)
  | inBit (x : ℕ) (e : Expr)
  | emit (e : Expr)
  | coin (x : ℕ)
  | half (x : ℕ) (e : Expr)
  deriving Repr

/-- A program of the extended language: the bodies of its procedures, numbered from 0. -/
abbrev XProgram : Type := List XStmt

/-- The vendored statements, as extended statements. -/
def XStmt.ofStmt : Light.Stmt → XStmt
  | .skip => .skip
  | .set x e => .set x e
  | .store a e => .store a e
  | .seq s₁ s₂ => .seq (ofStmt s₁) (ofStmt s₂)
  | .ite c s₁ s₂ => .ite c (ofStmt s₁) (ofStmt s₂)
  | .while c s => .while c (ofStmt s)
  | .call p args x => .call p args x

/-- The limits of a run, and the input: the real edit adds the field `input` to `Light.Limits`
itself, which no vendored file constructs (design §15c). -/
structure XLimits : Type extends Limits where
  /-- The input string, read in place by `inBit`. -/
  input : List Bool

/-- The value of the input bit at position `p`: `1` if `0 ≤ p` and the bit there is `true`,
`0` otherwise (in particular off the input). -/
def inBitVal (x : List Bool) (p : ℤ) : ℤ := if 0 ≤ p ∧ x.getD p.toNat false = true then 1 else 0

/-- `XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c`: within the limits `lim`, at nesting depth `d`, the statement
`s` of `P`, started in `σ`, ends in `σ'` after exactly `c` steps, having emitted the bits `o`
and consumed the coins `r`. The rules of `Light.Exec` with the two indices, and one rule for
each new statement; `coin` has a rule for each bit. -/
inductive XExec (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) :
    ℕ → XStmt → State → State → List Bool → List Bool → ℕ → Prop
  | skip {d σ} : XExec lim P d .skip σ σ [] [] 0
  | set {d σ x e} : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ →
      XExec lim P d (.set x e) σ { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (e.val σ) } [] []
        (e.cost + 1)
  | store {d σ a e} : a.Safe lim.toLimits σ → e.Safe lim.toLimits σ →
      lim.toLimits.Addr (a.val σ) →
      XExec lim P d (.store a e) σ
        { σ with mem := Function.update σ.mem (a.val σ).toNat (e.val σ) } [] []
        (a.cost + e.cost + 1)
  | seq {d σ σ' σ'' s₁ s₂ o₁ o₂ r₁ r₂ c₁ c₂} : XExec lim P d s₁ σ σ' o₁ r₁ c₁ →
      XExec lim P d s₂ σ' σ'' o₂ r₂ c₂ →
      XExec lim P d (.seq s₁ s₂) σ σ'' (o₁ ++ o₂) (r₁ ++ r₂) (c₁ + c₂)
  | iteTrue {d σ σ' c s₁ s₂ o r k} : c.Safe lim.toLimits σ → c.Holds σ →
      XExec lim P d s₁ σ σ' o r k → XExec lim P d (.ite c s₁ s₂) σ σ' o r (c.cost + 1 + k)
  | iteFalse {d σ σ' c s₁ s₂ o r k} : c.Safe lim.toLimits σ → ¬ c.Holds σ →
      XExec lim P d s₂ σ σ' o r k → XExec lim P d (.ite c s₁ s₂) σ σ' o r (c.cost + 1 + k)
  | whileFalse {d σ c s} : c.Safe lim.toLimits σ → ¬ c.Holds σ →
      XExec lim P d (.while c s) σ σ [] [] (c.cost + 1)
  | whileTrue {d σ σ' σ'' c s o₁ o₂ r₁ r₂ k₁ k₂} : c.Safe lim.toLimits σ → c.Holds σ →
      XExec lim P d s σ σ' o₁ r₁ k₁ → XExec lim P d (.while c s) σ' σ'' o₂ r₂ k₂ →
      XExec lim P d (.while c s) σ σ'' (o₁ ++ o₂) (r₁ ++ r₂) (c.cost + 1 + k₁ + k₂)
  | call {d σ σ' p args x body o r k} : (∀ e ∈ args, e.Safe lim.toLimits σ) → P[p]? = some body →
      d < lim.depth → XExec lim P (d + 1) body ⟨frame (args.map (·.val σ)), σ.mem⟩ σ' o r k →
      XExec lim P d (.call p args x) σ ⟨Function.update σ.loc x (σ'.loc 0), σ'.mem⟩ o r
        ((args.map Expr.cost).sum + 2 + k)
  | inBit {d σ x e} : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ →
      XExec lim P d (.inBit x e) σ
        { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (inBitVal lim.input (e.val σ)) } [] [] (e.cost + 1)
  | emit {d σ e} : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ →
      XExec lim P d (.emit e) σ σ [decide (e.val σ ≠ 0)] [] (e.cost + 1)
  | coin {d σ x} (b : Bool) :
      XExec lim P d (.coin x) σ { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (if b then 1 else 0) } []
        [b] 1
  | half {d σ x e} : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ →
      XExec lim P d (.half x e) σ { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (e.val σ / 2) } [] []
        (e.cost + 1)

/-! ## The six inductions over `Exec`, restated (the edit set extends each by the new cases) -/

section Inductions

variable {lim : XLimits} {P : XProgram} {d : ℕ} {s : XStmt} {σ σ' : State} {o r : List Bool}
  {c : ℕ}

/-- **Conservativity.** A run of the vendored language is a run of the extended language that
emits nothing and consumes no coin.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the vendored run, rule by rule. -/
theorem XExec.ofExec {P₀ : Light.Program} {s₀ : Light.Stmt}
    (h : Light.Exec lim.toLimits P₀ d s₀ σ σ' c) :
    XExec lim (P₀.map XStmt.ofStmt) d (XStmt.ofStmt s₀) σ σ' [] [] c := by
  sorry

/-- A run stays a run when procedures are appended (the extension of `Light.Exec.append`,
`Logic.lean:62`). -/
theorem XExec.append (h : XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c) (R : XProgram) :
    XExec lim (P ++ R) d s σ σ' o r c := by
  sorry

/-- The locals that a statement assigns: those of `Light.Stmt.assigns` (`Assigns.lean:43`), and
the targets of `inBit`, `coin` and `half`. -/
@[simp] def XStmt.assigns : XStmt → List ℕ
  | .skip => []
  | .set x _ => [x]
  | .store _ _ => []
  | .seq s t => s.assigns ++ t.assigns
  | .ite _ s t => s.assigns ++ t.assigns
  | .while _ s => s.assigns
  | .call _ _ x => [x]
  | .inBit x _ => [x]
  | .emit _ => []
  | .coin x => [x]
  | .half x _ => [x]

/-- A run leaves a local that the statement does not assign as it was (the extension of
`Light.Exec.loc_eq_of_notMem_assigns`, `Assigns.lean:54`). -/
theorem XExec.loc_eq_of_notMem_assigns {y : ℕ} (h : XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c)
    (hy : y ∉ s.assigns) : σ'.loc y = σ.loc y := by
  sorry

/-- A run that starts with words everywhere ends with words everywhere (the extension of
`Light.Exec.bounded`, `RunsStayInLimits.lean:83`). **New hypothesis** `1 ≤ lim.word`: `inBit`
and `coin` write `1`, which the vendored rules never do without a `Safe` premise; `Light.Std`
gives it (`100 ≤ word`). `half` needs nothing, since `|⌊v / 2⌋| ≤ |v|`. -/
theorem XExec.bounded (h : XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c) (hw : (1 : ℤ) ≤ lim.word)
    (hσ : σ.Bounded lim.toLimits) : σ'.Bounded lim.toLimits := by
  sorry

/-- A run does not change the cells from `lim.space` on (the extension of
`Light.Exec.mem_outside`, `RunsStayInLimits.lean:99`); the new statements change no cell. -/
theorem XExec.mem_outside (h : XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c) (a : ℕ) (ha : lim.space ≤ a) :
    σ'.mem a = σ.mem a := by
  sorry

/-- Each coin costs one step, so a run of `c` steps consumes at most `c` coins: streams of
length `c` suffice.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the run; every rule's cost is at least the sum of its parts'
plus, for `coin`, one. -/
theorem XExec.coins_length_le (h : XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c) : r.length ≤ c := by
  sorry

/-- Each emitted bit costs at least one step. -/
theorem XExec.output_length_le (h : XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c) : o.length ≤ c := by
  sorry

/-- **Determinism.** Two runs of the same statement from the same state whose consumed words are
both prefixes of one stream `ρ` are the same run: same final state, output, consumed word and
cost. Randomized acceptance (`acceptProb`) needs it (design §15c, obstacle 2).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the first run, inversion on the second. A test's outcome is a
function of the state, so both runs take the same rule. For `seq` and `whileTrue` the first
parts' consumed words are prefixes of `ρ`, so the induction hypothesis makes them equal; the
second parts then consume prefixes of the same rest of `ρ`. For `coin` the two bits are the
first bit of `ρ`. -/
theorem XExec.det {σ₁ σ₂ : State} {o₁ o₂ r₁ r₂ : List Bool} {c₁ c₂ : ℕ} {ρ : List Bool}
    (h₁ : XExec lim P d s σ σ₁ o₁ r₁ c₁) (h₂ : XExec lim P d s σ σ₂ o₂ r₂ c₂)
    (hr₁ : r₁ <+: ρ) (hr₂ : r₂ <+: ρ) : σ₁ = σ₂ ∧ o₁ = o₂ ∧ r₁ = r₂ ∧ c₁ = c₂ := by
  sorry

end Inductions

/-! ## The logic: `Ends` unchanged in type, `EndsIO` -/

/-- The statement `s`, started in `σ`, ends within `T` steps in a state that satisfies `Q`, for
some output and some consumed coins (hidden). The real edit redefines `Light.Ends` so, keeping
its type, so that `Light.Meets` and the vendored routines are untouched. For a statement with
coins this is an existential (some coin outcome): specifications that are to hold for every
stream use `EndsIO`. -/
def XEnds (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (d : ℕ) (s : XStmt) (σ : State) (T : ℕ)
    (Q : State → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ' o r c, XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c ∧ c ≤ T ∧ Q σ'

/-- `EndsIO lim P d s σ ρ T Q`: with the coin stream `ρ`, the statement `s`, started in `σ`,
ends within `T` steps in a state `σ'`, having emitted `o` and consumed a prefix `r` of `ρ`, with
`Q σ' o r`. By `XExec.det` there is at most one such run. -/
def EndsIO (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (d : ℕ) (s : XStmt) (σ : State) (ρ : List Bool) (T : ℕ)
    (Q : State → List Bool → List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ' o r c, XExec lim P d s σ σ' o r c ∧ r <+: ρ ∧ c ≤ T ∧ Q σ' o r

section Rules

variable {lim : XLimits} {P : XProgram} {d : ℕ} {σ : State} {ρ : List Bool} {T : ℕ}
  {Q : State → List Bool → List Bool → Prop}

/-- An `EndsIO` fact is an `Ends` fact. -/
theorem EndsIO.toXEnds {s : XStmt} {Q' : State → Prop} (h : EndsIO lim P d s σ ρ T Q)
    (hQ : ∀ σ' o r, Q σ' o r → Q' σ') : XEnds lim P d s σ T Q' := by
  sorry

/-- An `EndsIO` fact holds with more time and any weaker conclusion. -/
theorem EndsIO.mono {s : XStmt} {T' : ℕ} {Q' : State → List Bool → List Bool → Prop}
    (h : EndsIO lim P d s σ ρ T Q) (hT : T ≤ T') (hQ : ∀ σ' o r, Q σ' o r → Q' σ' o r) :
    EndsIO lim P d s σ ρ T' Q' := by
  sorry

/-- A statement of the vendored language: its `Ends` fact holds for every stream, with nothing
emitted and nothing consumed. The bridge that keeps the 14 routines usable under `EndsIO`. -/
theorem EndsIO.ofEnds {P₀ : Light.Program} {s₀ : Light.Stmt} {Q₀ : State → Prop}
    (h : Light.Ends lim.toLimits P₀ d s₀ σ T Q₀) :
    EndsIO lim (P₀.map XStmt.ofStmt) d (XStmt.ofStmt s₀) σ ρ T fun σ' o r =>
      Q₀ σ' ∧ o = [] ∧ r = [] := by
  sorry

/-- `skip` ends at once, in its start state, emitting and consuming nothing. -/
theorem EndsIO.skip (h : Q σ [] []) : EndsIO lim P d .skip σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- An assignment of a safe expression ends within its cost, emitting and consuming nothing. -/
theorem EndsIO.set {x : ℕ} {e : Expr} (hs : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ) (hT : e.cost + 1 ≤ T)
    (h : Q { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (e.val σ) } [] []) :
    EndsIO lim P d (.set x e) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- A store of a safe expression at an address within the limits ends within its cost, emitting
and consuming nothing. -/
theorem EndsIO.store {a e : Expr} (ha : a.Safe lim.toLimits σ) (he : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ)
    (hA : lim.toLimits.Addr (a.val σ)) (hT : a.cost + e.cost + 1 ≤ T)
    (h : Q { σ with mem := Function.update σ.mem (a.val σ).toNat (e.val σ) } [] []) :
    EndsIO lim P d (.store a e) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- Sequencing: the second statement runs on the rest of the stream, and the outputs and the
consumed words are concatenated. -/
theorem EndsIO.seq {s₁ s₂ : XStmt} (T₁ T₂ : ℕ)
    (h : EndsIO lim P d s₁ σ ρ T₁ fun σ' o₁ r₁ =>
      EndsIO lim P d s₂ σ' (ρ.drop r₁.length) T₂ fun σ'' o₂ r₂ => Q σ'' (o₁ ++ o₂) (r₁ ++ r₂))
    (hT : T₁ + T₂ ≤ T) : EndsIO lim P d (.seq s₁ s₂) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- A branch: the side that the test selects, on the same stream, after the test's cost. -/
theorem EndsIO.ite {c : Cond} {s₁ s₂ : XStmt} (T' : ℕ) (hs : c.Safe lim.toLimits σ)
    (h₁ : c.Holds σ → EndsIO lim P d s₁ σ ρ T' Q) (h₂ : ¬ c.Holds σ → EndsIO lim P d s₂ σ ρ T' Q)
    (hT : c.cost + 1 + T' ≤ T) : EndsIO lim P d (.ite c s₁ s₂) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- A loop whose test holds: one round on the stream, then the loop on the rest. -/
theorem EndsIO.whileStep {c : Cond} {s : XStmt} (T₁ T₂ : ℕ) (hs : c.Safe lim.toLimits σ)
    (hc : c.Holds σ)
    (h : EndsIO lim P d s σ ρ T₁ fun σ' o₁ r₁ =>
      EndsIO lim P d (.while c s) σ' (ρ.drop r₁.length) T₂ fun σ'' o₂ r₂ =>
        Q σ'' (o₁ ++ o₂) (r₁ ++ r₂))
    (hT : c.cost + 1 + T₁ + T₂ ≤ T) : EndsIO lim P d (.while c s) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- A loop whose test fails ends after the test, emitting and consuming nothing. -/
theorem EndsIO.whileDone {c : Cond} {s : XStmt} (hs : c.Safe lim.toLimits σ) (hc : ¬ c.Holds σ)
    (hQ : Q σ [] []) (hT : c.cost + 1 ≤ T) : EndsIO lim P d (.while c s) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- Calls: the body runs on the same stream; the output and the consumed coins pass through. -/
theorem EndsIO.call {p x : ℕ} {args : List Expr} {body : XStmt} (T' : ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ e ∈ args, e.Safe lim.toLimits σ) (hp : P[p]? = some body) (hd : d < lim.depth)
    (h : EndsIO lim P (d + 1) body ⟨frame (args.map (·.val σ)), σ.mem⟩ ρ T' fun σ' o r =>
      Q ⟨Function.update σ.loc x (σ'.loc 0), σ'.mem⟩ o r)
    (hT : (args.map Expr.cost).sum + 2 + T' ≤ T) : EndsIO lim P d (.call p args x) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- `x := inBit e` sets `x` to the input bit at the position `e` (`0` off the input), within
`e.cost + 1` steps, emitting and consuming nothing. -/
theorem EndsIO.inBit {x : ℕ} {e : Expr} (hs : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ) (hT : e.cost + 1 ≤ T)
    (h : Q { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (inBitVal lim.input (e.val σ)) } [] []) :
    EndsIO lim P d (.inBit x e) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- `emit e` emits the one bit "`e ≠ 0`" within `e.cost + 1` steps and changes no variable or
cell. -/
theorem EndsIO.emit {e : Expr} (hs : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ) (hT : e.cost + 1 ≤ T)
    (h : Q σ [decide (e.val σ ≠ 0)] []) : EndsIO lim P d (.emit e) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- A coin reads the first bit of the stream. -/
theorem EndsIO.coin {x : ℕ} {b : Bool} {ρ' : List Bool} (hρ : ρ = b :: ρ') (hT : 1 ≤ T)
    (h : Q { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (if b then 1 else 0) } [] [b]) :
    EndsIO lim P d (.coin x) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- `x := half e` sets `x` to `⌊e / 2⌋` within `e.cost + 1` steps, emitting and consuming
nothing. -/
theorem EndsIO.half {x : ℕ} {e : Expr} (hs : e.Safe lim.toLimits σ) (hT : e.cost + 1 ≤ T)
    (h : Q { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (e.val σ / 2) } [] []) :
    EndsIO lim P d (.half x e) σ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-- The `Ends` rule for a coin: some bit leads to `Q` (the existential reading of `Ends`). -/
theorem XEnds.coin {x : ℕ} {Q' : State → Prop} (b : Bool) (hT : 1 ≤ T)
    (h : Q' { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (if b then 1 else 0) }) :
    XEnds lim P d (.coin x) σ T Q' := by
  sorry

end Rules

/-! ## Specifications of procedures with input and output -/

/-- `MeetsIO lim P p d vals μ ρ T R`: procedure `p`, run at depth `d` on the arguments `vals` in
the memory `μ` with the stream `ρ`, ends within `T` steps with a result, a memory, an output and
a consumed word that satisfy `R`. The I/O counterpart of `Light.Meets` (`Calls.lean:57`), which
stays as it is. -/
def MeetsIO (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (p d : ℕ) (vals : List ℤ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (ρ : List Bool)
    (T : ℕ) (R : ℤ → (ℕ → ℤ) → List Bool → List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ body, P[p]? = some body ∧
    EndsIO lim P d body ⟨frame vals, μ⟩ ρ T fun σ' o r => R (σ'.loc 0) σ'.mem o r

/-- `x := p(args)` with a specification that sees the output and the coins (the I/O counterpart
of `Light.Ends.callLast`, `Calls.lean:113`). -/
theorem EndsIO.callLast {lim : XLimits} {P : XProgram} {d p x T T' : ℕ} {loc μ : ℕ → ℤ}
    {args : List Expr} {vals : List ℤ} {ρ : List Bool}
    {R : ℤ → (ℕ → ℤ) → List Bool → List Bool → Prop} {Q : State → List Bool → List Bool → Prop}
    (hp : MeetsIO lim P p (d + 1) vals μ ρ T' R)
    (h : ∀ v μ' o r, R v μ' o r → Q ⟨Function.update loc x v, μ'⟩ o r)
    (ha : (∀ e ∈ args, e.Safe lim.toLimits ⟨loc, μ⟩) ∧ args.map (·.val ⟨loc, μ⟩) = vals)
    (hd : d < lim.depth) (hT : (args.map Expr.cost).sum + 2 + T' ≤ T) :
    EndsIO lim P d (.call p args x) ⟨loc, μ⟩ ρ T Q := by
  sorry

/-! ## Acceptance -/

/-- The outermost statement of a whole program: procedure `p0` on the locals 1 and 2 (the copy
of `Light.mainStmt`, `ProgramCode.lean`, for the extended syntax). With `inLen` from an argument,
local 1 holds `|x|`. -/
def xmainStmt (p0 : ℕ) : XStmt := .call p0 [.var 1, .var 2] 0

/-- **Nondeterministic acceptance** (design §15c): some coin stream of length `T` makes the
outermost call, on `|x| = |lim.input|` and `j`, end within `T` steps with a positive result.
Time bounds are stated separately and uniformly over all streams, as `NTIME` and `NSPACE`
require. [AB09, §2.1.2] -/
def AcceptsND (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (p0 : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ ρ : List Bool, ρ.length = T ∧
    EndsIO lim P 0 (xmainStmt p0) ⟨frame [0, lim.input.length, j], μ⟩ ρ T fun σ' _ _ => 0 < σ'.loc 0

open Classical in
/-- **Randomized acceptance** (design §15c): the probability, over a uniform stream of `m` coins,
that the outermost call ends within `T` steps with a positive result. Well defined as a
probability of runs because the run of each stream is unique (`XExec.det`). [AB09, Def 7.2] -/
noncomputable def acceptProb (lim : XLimits) (P : XProgram) (p0 : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (μ : ℕ → ℤ)
    (m T : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  Randomized.randProb m fun ρ =>
    EndsIO lim P 0 (xmainStmt p0) ⟨frame [0, lim.input.length, j], μ⟩ ρ T fun σ' _ _ => 0 < σ'.loc 0

/-! ## The compiler's word-size condition -/

/-- `Light.Compiler.Fits` (`Cells.lean:79`) with the input-length clause of design §15c: the
input length fits the limit on words. (It is a condition on the limits, not on `W`; with
`Fits.word` it gives `InRange W |x|`, which the argument cell holding `|x|` needs. `inBit`
itself needs no such clause, since a position off the input reads `0`.) -/
structure XFits (W : ℕ) (lim : XLimits) (N Q : ℕ) : Prop
    extends Light.Compiler.Fits W lim.toLimits N Q where
  /-- The input length fits the limit on words. -/
  input_le : (lim.input.length : ℤ) ≤ lim.word

end TCSlib.Draft.Stage2.Lang
